Content: Place matters. We have navigated what it means to be in community with one another and the land. Living in a place allows us to receive the gifts of that place, but it's also a commitment to that place and its people. What do we contribute? As much as possible, we draw sustenance from that land and from local merchants (still having trouble thinking post-capitalism; maybe a barter system)?
We know people differently-not because we like everybody that we live around, but because we're sharing deep relationship to the place.
Taking care of people and land and water are central to survival. But once this need is resolved will we become as removed and superficial as them.
The lake will have taught us all to breath, and “Hopefully fox will still be tricking people”
We will have made the world safe for our bare feet.

“Place”
Some stay in place and have limited input and output
Some stay in place and welcome guests
Some stay in place and visit other places often…inoften
Some mostly visit other places but have a home place
Some are always wandering
Our environments are multi-colored with bright light. The connections between and among people are illuminated through deeper senses we have cultivated. Our awareness of all of this benefits us all.
Life is blooming, watered, connected. We have gotten good at bridging the gaps between hardships and possibility. We are part of the relationships with everything.
Any community is built around the landscape. We build around what is already there. For example–bridges are placed in the places where the water calls for them. It is much more calm.
Return to agriculture and stewardship. Ancestors said “Ewwww germs. We now say, “Wow, Biodiversity!”
The land holds us. This love holds us. Connects back to us holding the land. We are the ancestors.
A connection to the land and all living beings is valued over money and consumerism. Our traditional teachings guide those relationships.
There is intention around how and what we use and consume in our daily lives.

When describing my hood, I say something like “You know where the lush green and yellow and purple and violet and indigo and white and mauve and black plants are? That’s it beside and around the deposits of the Anacostia River? So when you get there, take a left at the house of people knowledge, climb down the stairs of the adult playground and cross the street to where the dogs are herding the children to the butterfly garden.”

Our histories and our future - the earth holds our stories; nothing is lost. 150 years into the future, perhaps we consciously nourish our awareness of cycles and connection to all things. We are on the lookout for important answers because we know they’re out there - held by the earth – even when the wisdom no longer exists in the written word – we access the stories through our connection with the earth.

All are kin, and we connect with one another with that as the basis of being. The earth has come back into a healthy state of being in response to the ways that we have changed. Our remembering our relationship to it has allowed it to re-member.
Everyone knows that no matter where we are, we are looking at the same moon. We are always connected.

Clouds = less boundaried geography. Weaving our communities together. Mt Tamalpais - more reciprocal relationship to nature and our role, less extractive, more connective. We have meetings sitting in trees.
I return to my country
Walking barefoot without hurting myself. Because touching the earth is so beautiful
Original of Translation: Caminar descalza sin dañarme. Porque tocar la tierra es tan lindo.

Content: People do walkabouts in the forest with trust. Plants offer their gifts more freely because they trust humans in deeper relationship.
We all know…I am from somewhere.

We all have relationship to things out of this world.  A cow’s skull, for example, says everything about who we are in relationship to ourselves, one another, and the whole universe.  We are connected, holding hands, with the sacred.

Date/Circle Name: 1/11/25 BIPOC outdoors - Maji ya Chai Two Harbors MN
Content: There is a globally shared value of being with place - the place you are in, and adapting to place as movement and migration occurs, learning its ways as opposed to forcing new places to conform to you.

What we wear is a product of the land and how we see ourselves. Clothing is how we communicate and are protected. Return to growing natural products of the land. 
When your hands move…(ask Laura for writing) Storytelling and cloth “telling and tela”
More connection to the Earth

Date/Circle Name: 2/1/25 St Louis Park, MN BIPOC The Coven
Content: People know that nature is healing and go to the river, deep relationships with water and plants.

Villages within watersheds, distinct, but connected, have a mycelial approach to sharing all nutrition needed by humans and organisms. Mentors are shared across villages and watersheds. Gatherings around food bring people from within watersheds and across watersheds together. Kids meet elders organically, and as they are drawn to particular elders and vocations, they are offered the chance to be mentored by them for particular roles: teachers, healers, growers, water keepers, crafts people. Food is local, and trading, gifting and bartering are everyday ways to move what's needed around. Songs are shared within and across watersheds. Animals are revered, and part of the community. They are known clearly, the deer with the limp and the blue jay that sneaks bread off the table. Young people participate in governance, their voices and dreams are heard with the same import as adults. Water is sacred. It’s woven into stories, songs and celebrations. There are families, and, they matter less, peeps just share in kidcare, not just to help “the kids and their parents” but because they are a source of nutrition for adults too. Healing circles are constantly convening, to keep peeps whole, metabolize traumas and address fractures.

Since there are far fewer of us, and we rely on each other more, we naturally concentrate ourselves into smaller areas. The animals, plants, and insects have a proper field day with all the freed-up land.
There is interconnectedness of place. People respect the places they live and also build interconnectedness with other places.
Amazing.  Out in the sea with the creatures and the good feeling as one.  Thanking the sun.  Thanking the water.  And there's an overall sense of well-being and connectedness within and without.
This is my rightful place. Mushroom journeys have helped me understand my place here.
The whole world is the waʻa

Boreal…northern region – Duluth… Delisting of the St. Louis River… fish, recreation, growing rice,. Vision: Racism is “delisted” a giant smile on my face, weight off my shoulders, peace in my heart; all generational curses broken. Drawing of a river…
We breathe so well.  It’s a cleaner environment.  Anxiety no longer catches our breath.  We have evolved out of allergies.
There is no such thing as an invasive species. We know where and why everyone is here.

There is a sunset over a sand beach, with a blue and purplish sky.  There are 3 birds flying through. The sun is a yellowish orange with a light purple setting. Dark blue water, two palm trees. I saw a young teen laying between two palm trees in the tree swing, with his little brother playing in the sand under him building sand castles, listening to the history of his long lost family from an elder of the family he just met.
We know the names of all the bodies of water around us, they know us too and we talk each day.
We danced in the rain and we swam in the rivers. And they all laughed

The planet has been healed. Sun is bright for everyone. There is no more stealing of land and no more borders. We live where we want, with no fear of being displaced. There is calm, peace, balance, and abundance. Food was in abundance as well as medicine. Many of us are involved in farming.

Date/Circle Name: 2/27/25 Redwood City and North Fair Oaks, CA Sobrato 2
Content: Our rivers and forests are protected.  There are trees everywhere.  Things that grow green are vibrant green.  Birds, fish, streams - teeming with life.  Everyone accesses these places, and the places are more healthy and connected because of it.  We know wisdom comes from this connection.

Date/Circle Name: 2/27/25 Redwood City and North Fair Oaks, CA Sobrato 2
Content: The landscape and the human made scapes coexist!  Johnson street commune village has housing in a semi circle space with BBQ, Soccer, water, communal space all within the semi-circle.  Nature and connection flows around both.  People flow in and out as needed – so do the animals.

We know our connection to the Earth, and our connection to community.  We respect nature.  We understand how to use power for the good of all.  We know that a reciprocal relationship is critical to everyone's well being.
People live close to nature - like the Avatar depicted in the old stories.

There is absolute deep listening at all levels.  Everyone is listening to nature, to themselves, to land, to water, to the minerals.  Nothing would share itself if it hasn’t been right.  There is reciprocity – circle processes help.  People share their gifts.
We live from an honorable harvest.  All living beings are kin.  We behave understanding that our presence is an offering.

We are so attuned with nature and the Universe’s algorithm. We can hear the plant kin and the animal kin. We practice deep listening. The rivers are connected to the lakes. We remember indigenous teachings about the natural highways through Turtle Island. We care for those corridors and for what the animals are already trying to map out for us through their migrations.

There is more space for those natural corridors to thrive and we are living in relationship with those. These algorithms interrupt the algorithms of technology.
We practice into an understanding that the Earth doesn’t belong to us, we belong to the Earth. We honor the children who will inherit the Earth.
We listen to the  sound of the wind, and the sounds of the rain.  There is good music and good food–with good rum spattered in there. We wake up to the morning refreshed.
We remember the places where these elements already existed on earth in 2025. We have connected more to those – the villages where children are free and parents don’t have to worry.

Where the rivers and the land meet is an emergent space. Caring and tending to that place where there is a living energy. The emergent space between the rivers becomes space for all the animals to move, where we learn about conflict and how to care and tend to the health and wellbeing of the emergent space so the animals can freely travel. Teachings from that space, calling us into that space is part of our education – learning what needs to be tended and harvested. 

There’s grit here in an open-hearted space where conflict is about opportunity. The arts are practices happening in all different places, in institutions and governments. Our imaginations are given space to thrive. 

We care for the edges.
We know where our food, materials, and nourishment come from
I walk out my front door (which is never locked) and see gardens, bicyclists, the sky, murals, a park full of children
We know the names of all the plants

The earth is spinning and all of its inhabitants have all that they need: food, love, care. Stewards hold the earth and play a role in ensuring everyone has that stuff. The oceans and land masses are places of being and becoming.
Everyone has access to water, food, resources, housing, etc. We are not attached to capitalism. We honor other living things and the lands the way that indigenous leaders teach us.
Feet are on the ground, warm feeling, welcomed as if you are home no matter where you are, what you look like, what you are wearing or what you are doing.  No fear.

We care deeply for the Earth.  Food is available everywhere. There are open spaces and wildlife everywhere. Butterflies across the land. Streams are clear, glittery, you can drink from them. There are lots of insects and amphibians. Bird song is present.
Water, shelter, and food are guaranteed.
NYC is an exciting place of exchange that smells good all year round.
As the surfer takes in the sun at the beach the mussels hang happily on the rocks, fresh & delicious.
Animals that need homes have homes.
People enjoy the sunset and sunrise.
Everyone orients to the new moon and full moon.  To the seasons and patterns of life.  There are ceremonies to keep us on track and honor.  There are aspects of food and play in everything we do.

Water is life, being outside, producing and growing, central spaces to come together
Nature is not something we go to – we are in and with nature
Collectives

Treehouses are awesome! Growing our own homes, express yourself in the way that you’re living
We have always lived near water
When the lights go out people go outside and dance under the moon.
I hope that ther is a sweet river with fish, a fire circle where diverse people share wisdom, where fresh air and birds exists, where sun is present and the land is never without cultivation
Original of Translation: Yo quiero que haya un rio dulce con peces, una fogata con diferentes personas compartiendo sabiduría, aire fresco, aves, que haya sol y que no falte el cultivo

Content: Sensations about - being in company, feeling the air, feeling the sun, mountains, plants, animals, everything in harmony

Inspired by a bike ride where a lot of birds were infront of me and overhead. An image- Abundance with no borders, everything is flowing, trees are huge, a woman and a child who are diverse are here simbolizing that diversity is respected, lifted up and celebrated.

I took mental fotos of the land the structures that are sustainable, apples, dahlias, bees on the poppies, the gathering spaces out there, the food that was prepared for us lovingly from what was picked, blue print on the wall of native peoples of the land, dogs at peace and comfortable and loved, and libraries- for me this place is what a thriving horizon looks like

The valuing of unique gifts, extends beyond people and over to places. Place is not transferable and when confronted with a challenge in one place, people choose to stay and meet the challenges in the places they know best because those relationships are so deep. People have moved from living in fear to living in the present.

Date/Circle Name: 10/29/25 Kailua, HI Kahanaiki Group, Le Jardin Academy
Content: The Hawaiian Islands are connected by water and shared stories. Hawaii is green and ʻāina-centered, where we appreciate how important our land is

Date/Circle Name: 10/30/25 Kailua, HI Kipuka Pala'a Group, Le Jardin Academy
Content: This island becomes more than just one of the Hawaiian Islands. This land will become a true glimpse of paradise: preserved natural elements. Our descendants are taught the stories of the past, picking up new stories on the way. Our descendants will be able to look out into the horizon and not have to worry about problems like pollution or war. Hawaiʻi is a safe haven. Water is everything.

Date/Circle Name: 10/30/25 Kailua, HI Kipuka Pala'a Group, Le Jardin Academy
Content: This island has reverted back to the old ways. It can provide for itself and its people. Our children and our children’s children pass down our stories to the next generations, all while creating their own stories. They made changes in the way we lived and taught the importance of taking care of the land we live on. Our descendants learned from their parents and teachers to respect themselves and each other. To come together to take care of our planet.

Date/Circle Name: 10/30/25 Kailua, HI Polynesian Club, Le Jardin Academy
Content: People are excited to be aware of the geological knowledge of the land they live on. Everyday life doesn’t throw the natural world under the bus.

Date/Circle Name: 10/30/25 Kailua, HI Polynesian Club, Le Jardin Academy
Content: In this thriving horizon it is a world where everyone is versed in their native ecosystem’s ways of thriving, and online media is used to share each other’s cultures and explore the natural knowledge of other areas around the world.
Everyone has space they are responsible for and steward together - forest, shoreline, farm…
Parks are not only meeting spaces, but also a place for all kinds of play for both adults and children. We come together to play, meet, and then play again!
Lush lands and flowing rivers where children play and learn and see their ancestors faces in the rain clouds
I see folx feeling grounded in their surroundings comforted by trees, their gardens and nature. I see children drinking fresh water from mountain springs and splashing each other

From pain and sadness, tears fill lakes and there are people tending to the sorrow and pain. The pain goes to the clouds and sky and is turned into archives that fall down and people catch them. The land is split, being changed as a result of collective learning, which becomes the building blocks for the built environment – based on the archive of truth and knowledge.

There is now land ownership, only  land stewardship. You only get to live at a place like the beach or the woods if you’ve learned how to steward and care for that land and become part of the community that lives there. There’s people moving around but you must be taken under someone’s wing to be able to inhabit land so that you can take care of it.

A rainbow for everyone. All cultures holding hands. A river that I love. Hearing the trickle of the water when it is flowing. The family playing soccer with the trees, the free butterflies, next to the river. We have horses, and the children are on bicycles. The elderly walk holding hands.
Original of Translation:
Un arcoiris para todos. Todas las culturas agarradas de la mano. Un rio que me encanta. Escuchar el chorrito del agua cuando esta fluyendo. La familia jugando futbol con los arboles, las mariposas libres, al lado del rio. Tenemos caballos y los niños en bicicleta. Los ancianos caminan agarraditos de la mano. 

Una paz en nuestra vida sin tanta maldad.

Content: I was a little bird. I was in the water. The water, the fish, and the people who consume them. Let us restore life in the rivers, so that we have fish again. Consuming food and putting water into our body.
Original of Translation: Spirituality gives us hope, faith, believing in family, in people.

Content: Inner childhood, lake, a barkhouse, redwoods, ocean, storms, red clay, red earth, blue skies, a spiral- Symbol for going forward and backward-inward and outward, balance. Rainbow people.

My people, comanche, for us the last tribes to be forced into submission, at the beginning of developing as a nation, tribe as business, buffalo restoration went terribly-I’d like to see the buffalo restored on the plains. The horse is reclaimed-they are lords of the plains because we used it to fight for so long. Comanche Fair- every year- change perspective on how we want to be- not as a business or economic powerhouse- return to our cultural ways- my sons being integrated and knowing who they are. Mt. Scott- Cultural Continuance

I see healing of relationship to nature- return to nature, revitalization of keystone species like buffalo and other animal relatives- what I pray for…the ability of children to have relationships to the world around them. If that can happen then all of the work of protectors has been successful

Everything I do is driven by vision- that vision of driving through my homelands and reclaiming - what if our development wasn’t interrupted by violence?  Sustainable housing that is made in a way that blends in with the landscape and brings healing to family networks, restoring relationship with food systems and food scapes, harvest to take care of the medicines and the foods, working towards no borders, we all have overlapping relationships with landscapes and sacred sites.

Lemon Tree- taking pictures to remember this, a picture of me and a rose. Succulents are so beautiful. I love them, I appreciate them. Hummingbirds living their best life. How often do we take the time to sit. Your stories, successes, your life is so beautiful. Bed with eachother, waking up with eachother, The beauty of nature and self care- self care is beautiful. The laughter in the air.

Fire and healing village- I hold a fire there. Sometimes fire is all we have. It's gonna be here for many generations. The elders and innerconnetedness, I went to a time of how it used to be- peace and harmony, elders around and children running freely. Felt really good. There was no homelessness. Every reservation had their own schooling. Tribal people running their own justice systems. Everyone helping eachother, a lot of elders in my community. Healthy relatives helping eachother

When I start praying, whatever wants me to know will come to me. Alcatraz- my love, my hate, my everything. Keep that story alive for our ppl. I’ve carried my daughter to alcatraz at 5, she’ll be 45 in August. I’m not doing this. 
She would never carry on. I got the vision that my daughter will carry our family story- the alcatraz story will continue carry on. Richard Oakes and proclamation -turning into education center. The museum is up and I envisioned that my daughter with the help of other alcatraz descendants will make it the cultural center that was in the original proclamation

Cherokee hills, creator’s beauty, if we take care of the land, prescribed burns, brought back bison and buffalo, bring back our language, language classes, accelerating in health, opened a hospital this year.
Future looks like a mirror of the opposite of what we are currently experiencing. What does it look like on the opposite horizon.
Bright sun, lots of trees. A river, houses with a bridge connecting them. Grass and birds flying
Sketch of a summer day. Happy children, spending fun time, frolicking at the beach

Date/Circle Name: 8/18/26 A New Way of Life Los Angeles
Content: And will be once again as a people that was here before us, left to live off the land to hunt, forage, and go back to the beginning.

Date/Circle Name: 8/18/26 A New Way of Life Los Angeles
Content: We are one people on one world–living in peace, harmony, and love.
We feel free to enjoy nature without feeling afraid.
Original of Translation: Nos sentimos libres de poder disfrutar de la naturaleza sin sentir el medio.

Content: We recognize that the earth is a living being and our home, and that is why we care for it.
Original of Translation: Reconocemos que la tierra es un ser vivo y nuestro hogar y por eso la cuidamos.

Content:
Our world is desolate.
Our world is bountiful.
Our world is harsh.
Our world is beautiful.
